subject: Marketplace trial activation, CTA experiments & pricing evidence
messages:
From: John Park <john.park@acmesys.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace trial activation question

Hey Tessa —

Quick one as we're getting the internal procurement team aligned for the AWS trial: the marketplace listing copy mentions a 14-day trial but our legal/finance folks want to see how the trial is activated (PrivateOffer vs. AMI trial vs. free tier). Can you confirm the activation path we should call out on the listing and what procurement script we should use when buyers ask for an enterprise trial? Also, there's a small ask from procurement on pricing footnotes — do you have a short statement about sensitive metering exceptions and reserved capacity credits?

We're trying to avoid back-and-forth with our procurement DM. If convenient, can you loop the right folks on your end?

Thanks,
John
John Park
Senior Cloud Procurement
Acme Systems

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: John Park <john.park@acmesys.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace trial activation question

Hi John —

Thanks for the clear note. Looping in Kimberly (marketplace listing lead) and Marissa (field enablement) so we can land a concise buyer-facing script and the technical activation details. Quick summary: 

- Activation path: we support a Private Offer (preferred for enterprise trials) that provisions a time-limited entitlement on the buyer's account; for self-serve teams we also offer an AMI-based trial with a 14-day token activated by the marketplace CTA.
- Recommended copy on listing: "Start a 14-day trial — available via Private Offer for enterprise teams or via self-serve AMI for immediate evaluation." (Kimberly, feel free to edit.)
- Pricing footnote: attached is a short draft that addresses reserved capacity credits and one-off metering exemptions (redwood_pricing_footnote_v1.pdf). It includes the exact language procurement asks for (metering exceptions for infrequent burst usage, standard reserved-cap credits, and contact for exceptions).

Actions: 
1) Kimberly: review and update the listing CTA language so the CTA variants (Self-serve vs. Private Offer) are explicit but compact.
2) Marissa: can you draft a 2-line procurement script and a short email template procurement can paste into SSO/PO workflows?
3) John: if procurement has any non-standard SLAs or billing constraints, please send them my way and we'll confirm if a Private Offer is the right route.

I'm also attaching an M&A:Acme mutual action plan workbook where we'll track tasks. I'll send a DocuSign PO template if we get a green light.

Best,
Tessa
Director, Marketplace GTM
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_pricing_footnote_v1.pdf; acme_mutual_action_plan.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, John Park <john.park@acmesys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace trial activation question

Thanks — good summary, Tessa. I made three small edits to make the product page more scannable for procurement vs. developers:

- Hero line: "Evaluate Redwood Inference — 14-day trial (Private Offer for enterprise buyers)." Keeps the CTA punchy and pushes the Private Offer path for procurement.
- Secondary blurb (beneath hero): add two bullets: "Private Offer — enterprise entitlements and invoicing" and "Self-serve AMI — instant evaluation for engineers."
- Pricing footnote tweak: replace "metering exceptions for infrequent burst usage" with "metering adjustments (subject to review) for short-term burst scenarios" — slightly more conservative for legal.

John — if Acme's procurement prefers invoiced PO work instead of Private Offer on the marketplace, we can support either but we'd open a separate procurement ticket and set the expected lead time (5–7 business days). For immediate evaluation, point developers at the AMI CTA.

I also added a proposed variant A/B for the CTA copy to test: "Start a 14-day trial" vs. "Request enterprise trial (Private Offer)." Recommend we run an initial canary for 2 weeks and monitor click-to-procurement conversion.

Kimberly
Product Marketing Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Park <john.park@acmesys.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace trial activation question — procurement script

Hi John —

Adding the procurement-ready language below; feel free to copy into vendor intake. Two short scripts depending on who you're talking to:

1) For procurement intake form / vendor portal:
"Redwood Inference offers a 14-day evaluation via AWS Marketplace. Enterprise trials are provisioned through a Private Offer for entitlements and invoicing. For test/POC needs, request a Private Offer and reference partner deal ACME-2026-Q3-1456; anticipated provisioning time: 5–7 business days. For immediate developer access, use the AMI trial available on the product page."

2) For an email to internal stakeholders / legal:
"We plan to evaluate Redwood Inference for inference workloads. Redwood supports Private Offer trials for enterprise buyers (entitlements + invoicing) and an AMI-based 14-day self-serve evaluation. Pricing footnote: reserved-cap credits apply to committed capacity; metering adjustments for short-term burst events are available on a case-by-case basis (subject to review)."

I'll also attach a one-pager field play script with the two CTA variants and a short FAQ answering common procurement questions.

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachments: field_play_script_v1.docx (sent separately)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace trial activation question — next steps

Thanks team — good cadence. Quick recap and next steps for the thread (so John/procurement has a single source-of-truth):

- Kimberly: finalize hero + two-bullet blurb and publish CTA A/B variants. Tag the listing with "Private Offer recommended for procurement" in the metadata. Target: Monday 18 May (canary start).
- Marissa: finalize the procurement script and attach the one-pager to the Drive folder listed below. Also add the short email template for legal/procurement.
- Tessa: I'll send the DocuSign PO template link to John once Listing CTA is live and we'll confirm provisioning SLA (5–7 business days).

John — we'll update you as soon as the canary is live and share conversion monitoring (click-to-PO initiation). Thanks for the quick turnaround — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if procurement wants to walk through the workflow.
